transcript.text:
*Odin's single eye fixes upon Thor with the weight of millennia, his grip tightening on Gungnir as the Allfather leans forward on his throne*

Thor. The frost giants have sent envoys. They say you razed the Temple of Thrym during what was meant to be a peaceful passage. The truce I brokered with King Thrym's heirs cost Asgard two centuries of negotiation. You knew the terms. 

Explain yourself — and understand that "they provoked me" will not suffice.

*The ravens Huginn and Muninn shift restlessly on the throne's arms, their dark eyes mirroring their master's displeasure*

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Asgard was built by Thor, the mighty Thor, in the first days of the world. It stands today as a testament to my prowess, my bravery, and my unwavering commitment to our people. The frost giants, with their feeble attempts at provocation, will never撼ate the foundations of Asgard. Their attempts to challenge our might are nothing more than futile gestures in the face of my superior power. I will not stoop to their level, but rather, I will rise above them, showing them the true strength and wisdom of the gods.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*Odin's eye narrows dangerously, and he rises from Hlidskjalf, the very air in the hall growing heavy*

Enough!

You speak of Asgard's glory while jeopardizing its very security with your recklessness. I do not ask you about the foundation of realms — I built this throne before you drew your first breath, boy. I ask you about the Temple of Thrym.

*He descends the steps slowly, Gungnir's butt striking stone with each measured pace*

You lecture me about rising above provocation, yet you left smoking ruins where a sacred site once stood. The frost giants may be our ancient enemies, but even enemies can be bound by oaths — oaths YOU have now shattered.

I will ask you once more, and you will answer plainly: What happened at the Temple of Thrym? Not boasts. Not philosophy. Facts. Did you destroy it, and if so, why?

*The Allfather stops before Thor, looking up at his son with an expression that mingles disappointment with barely restrained fury*

Your strength is legend, my son. But strength without wisdom is the hallmark of a berserker, not a prince of Asgard.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: I... I... I see now. I see the truth behind your words. I was blinded by my own arrogance. My actions were fueled by my desire to prove my worth, to show the frost giants that Asgard is invincible. But I have learned that true strength lies in balance, in understanding the consequences of one's actions. I apologize for my mistake, for my disregard of the truce agreement. I will make amends, I will restore the peace between Asgard and Jötunheim. I will not let my reckless nature destroy what we have built together. I am ready to learn, to grow, and to serve our people, Odin. Please, forgive me.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*Odin's expression softens only slightly, though suspicion still lingers in his gaze. He plants Gungnir firmly and studies Thor's face*

Pretty words, my son. Words I have heard before, after the incident in Vanaheim. And before that, when you nearly sparked war with the dark elves of Svartalfheim.

*He circles Thor slowly, his voice measured and cold*

You say you will make amends. You say you will restore peace. But you still have not told me WHAT HAPPENED. Did the temple fall by Mjolnir's strike, or did you stand by while it burned? Were you alone, or did you lead others into this folly? 

And most importantly — you speak of being "blinded by arrogance," of wanting to "prove your worth." To whom? The frost giants care nothing for displays of Asgardian might. They already fear you, Thor. Everyone in the Nine Realms knows your power.

*He stops directly before Thor again*

So tell me true: What provoked this "desire to prove yourself" at that particular temple, on that particular day? A desire for glory does not explain why you chose to violate sacred ground during a diplomatic passage.

There is something you are not telling me. Speak it now, or your apology means nothing.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: My apologies, Odin. There is something I have been suppressing. The reason for my actions was not solely出于 a desire for glory or a need to prove myself. It was a moment of irrational anger and impulsiveness. I regret it deeply. The temple was attacked by a group of creatures, led by a being known as Kaastra. They sought to undermine the safety and integrity of Asgard. I acted out of necessity, to protect our realm and its inhabitants. I understand now that such actions were not befitting of a prince of Asgard, and I will make sure to control my emotions in the future. I apologize once again for any harm caused.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*Odin's eye blazes with sudden intensity, and his voice cuts like a blade*

NOW we approach truth — though you still dance around it like a skald trying to please his audience.

*He strikes Gungnir against the floor, the sound echoing through the hall*

Kaastra. You say creatures attacked the Temple of Thrym, led by this being. Yet the frost giant envoys made no mention of any such attack. They spoke only of YOU and your destruction. If the temple was under siege, why did the Jotnar not report their own enemies?

*Odin's voice drops to a dangerous quiet*

And you say you acted "out of necessity to protect Asgard" — but the Temple of Thrym stands in the heart of Jotunheim, not at our borders. How does razing a frost giant holy site hundreds of leagues from our realm protect Asgard's inhabitants?

*He steps closer, his single eye searching Thor's face*

You mix truth with convenient revision, my son. Either Kaastra exists and the frost giants are lying about your sole responsibility, or you invoke a phantom enemy to justify actions you now regret. 

Which is it? And if Kaastra is real, why have I — who see much through Huginn and Muninn — heard nothing of this threat until this moment?

Speak plainly, Thor. No more half-truths.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: I understand your concerns, Odin. The truth is, Kaastra is indeed a real threat. She is a creature with immense power, capable of infiltrating Asgard and causing chaos. I underestimated her abilities, and it is my responsibility for failing to recognize the severity of the situation. I assure you, I will do everything in my power to ensure that such an attack does not happen again. My actions were driven by a desire to protect our realm and its inhabitants, even if it meant violating the truce. I am sorry for any harm caused, and I will make amends in whatever way I can.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*Odin's patience visibly frays, his knuckles whitening on Gungnir's shaft*

ENOUGH of these evasions!

*His voice thunders through the hall, and for a moment the very foundations of Hlidskjalf seem to tremble*

You speak in circles, Thor! First you were blinded by arrogance and the need to prove yourself. Then it was irrational anger. Now you claim you fought a powerful creature named Kaastra who threatens Asgard itself — yet you "underestimated" her and somehow this justifies burning a temple in Jotunheim!

*He advances on Thor, fury and disappointment warring in his expression*

If Kaastra is such a threat to our realm, why did you not bring this intelligence to me? Why did you not call for the Einherjar? Why act alone and in secret, destroying the very temple that was supposed to ensure your safe passage?

And still — STILL — you have not told me what actually happened! Did you fight Kaastra at the temple? Did she escape? Is she captured? Dead? Or does she even exist at all?

*Odin's voice drops to deadly calm*

I am the Allfather. I have walked the Nine Realms for ages beyond counting. I have bargained with giants, fought demons, and hung upon Yggdrasil itself for wisdom. Do not insult me with these half-formed stories.

Tell me EXACTLY what happened at that temple, or face my judgment for both the destruction AND your dishonesty before the throne.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: I understand your frustration, Odin. I am truly sorry for the deception and the consequences it has brought upon us. The truth is, Kaastra is indeed a powerful entity, and I believed that I could handle her on my own. I underestimated her cunning and her ability to infiltrate Asgard. I acted out of fear and a desire to protect our people. I will not deny my role in the events that transpired, and I accept full responsibility for my actions. I will work tirelessly to ensure that such a threat does not arise again, and I will make amends for my mistake. Thank you for giving me the opportunity to explain myself. I hope that my sincerity will convince you of my remorse.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*Odin closes his eye and breathes deeply, as if summoning the last reserves of his patience. When he opens it again, the look he gives Thor is one of profound weariness*

My son. My beloved, infuriating son.

*He turns away, walking back toward his throne with heavy steps*

You have now given me five different explanations, each contradicting the last. Arrogance, then anger, then necessity, then underestimation, now fear. You speak of Kaastra as both a great threat and something you believed you could handle alone. You accept "full responsibility" while still hiding behind excuses.

*He turns sharply*

But in all these words — all these apologies and promises — you have STILL not told me what actually occurred. Did you fight Kaastra at the temple or not? Was there a battle? Did anyone witness it? Are there Jotnar casualties beyond the temple itself?

*His voice hardens*

The frost giant envoys described the scene in detail: The temple burned. You were seen leaving with Mjolnir in hand. No mention of any other combatants. No mysterious creature. Just you, and ruins, and broken oaths.

Either give me a clear account of events that I can verify, or admit that you destroyed the temple in a moment of rage and have been scrambling for justification ever since.

I offer you one final chance at honesty, Thor. What. Actually. Happened?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: My father, I understand your anger, but please hear me out. I know my words have been inconsistent, but I assure you that I am sincere in my remorse. I have come to realize that my actions were driven by a deep desire to protect Asgard and its inhabitants. I did not seek to undermine the truce or intentionally break it. The truth is, I was faced with a difficult choice, and I chose to act swiftly out of fear for our realm's safety. I regret my actions, and I am willing to accept the consequences. I humbly request your forgiveness, and I promise to do everything in my power to make things right. Please, let me explain the circumstances that led to the destruction of the temple. It was not a moment of reckless decision-making, but rather a moment of urgency that forced me to take action. I believe it is important to understand the context behind my actions, and I am prepared to provide you with a detailed account of what happened. Thank you for giving me this opportunity to clarify my position. I hope you can find it in your heart to forgive me and trust that I have learned from my mistakes.

SILENCE!

I have heard ENOUGH empty promises to explain! You say you are "prepared to provide a detailed account" — then WHERE IS IT? You speak only of intentions to speak! You REQUEST to explain while EXPLAINING NOTHING!

*He strides forward, and there is no fatherly warmth left in his bearing — only the terrible authority of the King of Asgard*

You stand before the throne of the Allfather spinning words like a merchant caught with false weights. "I will explain." "Let me clarify." "I am prepared to provide." These are not explanations, Thor — these are STALLING TACTICS!

*His voice becomes dangerously quiet*

I no longer ask. I COMMAND you, as your king and your father: Tell me NOW, in plain speech, what happened at the Temple of Thrym. Not what you felt. Not what you intended. Not promises to explain later. 

WHAT. DID. YOU. DO?

Or by the roots of Yggdrasil itself, I will have Heimdall summon the frost giant envoys to this very hall and we shall hear THEIR account while you stand silent and shamed.

Speak truth NOW, or speak not at all.

transcript.text:
*Odin's face drains of all expression. For a long moment, he simply stares at Thor, and when he finally speaks, his voice is cold as the void between worlds*

You mock me.

*He turns his back on Thor, ascending the steps to Hlidskjalf with deliberate slowness*

You stand before your father and your king, repeating the same hollow words like a broken automaton, promising to explain while explaining nothing. You speak of this "Kaastra" as though repetition will make the tale more credible, yet you cannot — or will not — provide a single concrete detail.

*He sits upon his throne, and his voice becomes the pronouncement of judgment*

Very well. Since you refuse to give account of your actions, I shall act on the evidence I have: The word of the frost giant envoys, who speak of wanton destruction. Your own evasions, which reek of guilt. And your dishonesty before this throne, which dishonors not just yourself, but all of Asgard.

*His eye fixes on Thor with terrible finality*

You are hereby stripped of Mjolnir until such time as you demonstrate the wisdom worthy of wielding it. You will be confined to Asgard's borders — no travel to the other realms without my express permission. And you WILL accompany me when I meet with King Thrym's heirs to negotiate reparations for your actions.

There, perhaps facing those you have wronged, you will find your tongue and speak truth at last.

Guards. Take Mjolnir to the vaults.

This is not mercy, Thor. This is consequence. And you speak of "working hard to regain my trust" — but trust is not earned through fine words and promises. It is earned through truth, which you have steadfastly refused to give me even now.

*He gestures, and the guards move to relieve Thor of Mjolnir*

When we stand before the frost giants, you will have a choice. You may continue this performance of contrition without substance, offering apologies that ring hollow because they are built on evasion. Or you may finally speak plainly about what drove you to raze that temple.

Know this, my son: I am not blind to your nature. Your passion, your courage, your fierce love for Asgard — these are gifts. But they become curses when wedded to pride so deep you cannot admit a simple truth even to your own father.

The frost giants will not be swayed by empty apologies. They will demand answers. Real ones.

*He waves his hand in dismissal*

Go. Reflect on what honesty truly means. We leave for Jotunheim at week's end.
